(A) Like Hokusai's The Great Wave off Kanagawa, Hiroshige's Sudden Shower is a ukiyo-e woodblock print.
(B) Hokusai made The Great Wave around 1831, while Hiroshige made Sudden Shower in 1857.
(C) Hiroshige's Sudden Shower shows people crossing a bridge in a rainstorm.
(D) Hokusai's print shows a huge wave, whereas Hiroshige's shows a bridge in a rainstorm.
cards.a: (A). A similarity needs both prints and something they share: each is a ukiyo-e woodblock print, and "Like..." makes that shared feature the point. (B) and (D) set the prints against each other, emphasizing differences. (C) describes only one print.
cards.h: → letter + both prints + the shared feature
cards.n: (D) describes both prints most vividly, but "whereas" makes it a contrast.

cards.q:
A student has taken these notes:
• The Murchison meteorite fell in Australia in 1969.
• It contains tiny grains of silicon carbide.
• Some of the grains formed as long as about 7 billion years ago, in stars older than the Sun.
• The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago.
The student wants to emphasize how old some of the meteorite's grains are compared with the Sun. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
(A) The Murchison meteorite fell in Australia in 1969.
(B) The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago.
(C) The Murchison meteorite contains tiny grains of silicon carbide.
(D) Some grains in the Murchison meteorite formed as long as about 7 billion years ago, billions of years before the Sun.
cards.a: (D). The goal compares the grains' age with the Sun's, and (D) gives the grains' age and sets it against the Sun's formation. (A) gives the date the meteorite fell, not the grains' age. (C) names the grains without an age. (B) gives the Sun's age without the grains.
cards.h: → letter + both ages in one comparison
cards.n: (A) contains a date, which can pass for "age"; 1969 is when the meteorite fell, not how old its grains are.

cards.q:
A student has taken these notes:
• Construction of the bell tower in Pisa, Italy, began in 1173.
• The tower began to lean during construction.
• The lean was caused by soft, unstable soil under one side of the foundation.
• A pause in construction of nearly a century let the soil settle.
• From 1990 to 2001, engineers reduced the lean by removing soil from under the higher side.
The student wants to explain why the tower began to lean. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
(A) The bell tower in Pisa, begun in 1173, started to lean during construction.
(B) From 1990 to 2001, engineers reduced the lean by removing soil from under the higher side.
(C) The tower began to lean because the soil under one side of its foundation was soft and unstable.
(D) A pause in construction of nearly a century let the soil under the tower settle.
cards.a: (C). "Why" asks for a cause, and (C) gives it with "because": soft, unstable soil under one side. (A) says when the lean began, not why. (B) explains how the lean was reduced. (D) explains why the tower survived its lean, not why it leaned.
cards.n: (D) has a cause-and-effect structure of its own, but it explains a different effect.

cards.q:
A student has taken these notes:
• The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway opened in 2008.
• It stores backup copies of seeds from gene banks worldwide, in case the originals are lost.
• In 2015, seeds were first withdrawn, to rebuild a collection cut off by war in Syria.
• It can hold 4.5 million samples.
The student wants to explain the vault's purpose and give an example of it in action. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
(A) The Svalbard vault, which opened in Norway in 2008, can hold 4.5 million samples.
(B) The Svalbard vault stores backup seeds from gene banks worldwide; in 2015, for example, some were withdrawn to rebuild a collection cut off by war in Syria.
(C) In 2015, seeds were withdrawn from the Svalbard vault for the first time.
(D) Gene banks worldwide send backup seed samples to the Svalbard vault.
cards.a: (B). It states the purpose (backup copies in case originals are lost) and an example of that purpose at work (the 2015 withdrawal to rebuild a collection cut off by war). (A) gives place, date and capacity. (C) gives the event without its reason. (D) restates the purpose without an example.
cards.n: (C) is the example, but without the reason for the withdrawal it does not show the purpose being served.

cards.q:
A student has taken these notes:
• Psychologist Mei Tanaka surveyed 1,200 adults about sleep and mood.
• Those who reported sleeping under six hours a night had lower average mood scores.
• Sleep hours were self-reported, not measured with devices.
• Tanaka recommends that future studies use sleep trackers.
The student wants to present the study's main finding while acknowledging a limitation of its method. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
(A) Tanaka surveyed 1,200 adults about sleep and mood.
(B) Adults who reported sleeping under six hours a night had lower average mood scores.
(C) Because sleep hours were self-reported, Tanaka recommends that future studies use sleep trackers.
(D) In Tanaka's survey, adults reporting under six hours of sleep a night had lower average mood scores, though sleep hours were self-reported.
cards.a: (D). It gives the finding (short sleepers had lower mood scores) and the limitation (sleep hours were self-reported, not measured). (B) gives the finding with no limitation. (C) gives the limitation but no finding. (A) gives only the study's outline.
cards.n: (B) is the cleanest statement of the finding, and "main finding" is the half of the goal where students stop reading.

cards.q: If 4x − 6y = 18 and 5x + 2y = 11, what is the value of 9x − 4y?
cards.a: 29. Add the equations: (4x − 6y) + (5x + 2y) = 18 + 11, so 9x − 4y = 29. Solving for x and y first works but is slow and error-prone here: x = 51/19 and y = −23/19.
cards.n: Solving for x (51/19) and stopping, or grinding out both variables and slipping on a fraction; read what the question asks for before you start.

cards.q: In the system 3x + ky = 7 and 6x − 10y = 5, k is a constant. For what value of k does the system have no solution?
cards.a: −5. No solution means parallel lines: the same slope, different intercepts. The x-coefficients are in ratio 3 : 6 = 1 : 2, so k : (−10) must also be 1 : 2, giving k = −5. Check: 3x − 5y = 7 doubled is 6x − 10y = 14 ≠ 5, so the lines are parallel and distinct.
cards.n: Dropping the sign and entering 5, which makes the lines intersect; negative SPR answers need the minus sign typed in.

cards.q: In the equation 4(ax − 3) = 12x + b, a and b are constants. If the equation has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of a + b?
cards.a: −9. Expand: 4ax − 12 = 12x + b. Infinitely many solutions means both sides are identical, so 4a = 12 (a = 3) and b = −12. Then a + b = 3 + (−12) = −9.
cards.n: Writing b = 12 from "−12 = b" read carelessly, which gives 15; the question also asks for a + b, not a or b.

cards.q: A freight elevator can carry at most 1,600 pounds. An operator who weighs 190 pounds rides with crates that weigh 65 pounds each. What is the greatest number of crates the elevator can carry on one trip?
cards.a: 21. 190 + 65c ≤ 1,600 gives 65c ≤ 1,410, so c ≤ 21.69... The number of crates must be a whole number that does not exceed the limit, so c = 21. Check: 190 + 65(21) = 1,555 ≤ 1,600, while 22 crates give 1,620 > 1,600.
cards.h: → integer + check the one above it
cards.n: Rounding 21.69 to 22 breaks the "at most" limit; with a maximum, round down, and check the next integer up.

cards.q: A student's scores on four tests are 88, 92, 79, and 85. What is the least integer score on a fifth test that would make the average of the five scores greater than 87?
cards.a: 92. The four scores total 344. The average must exceed 87: (344 + s)/5 > 87 gives 344 + s > 435, so s > 91. The least integer greater than 91 is 92. A score of 91 gives an average of exactly 87, which is not greater than 87.
cards.n: Entering 91 by solving the equation (344 + s)/5 = 87; "greater than" is strict, so the boundary value fails.

cards.q: The volume of water V, in liters, in a tank t minutes after it begins to drain is given by V = 840 − 35t. How many minutes after the tank begins to drain does it hold one-fourth of its initial volume?
cards.a: 18. The initial volume is 840 liters, and one-fourth of it is 210. Solve 840 − 35t = 210: 35t = 630, so t = 18. (6 minutes is when a quarter of the water has drained, not when a quarter remains.)
cards.n: Entering 6, the time to drain 210 liters; "holds one-fourth" means 210 liters remain, so 630 liters have drained.

cards.q: The solution to the system 2x + 7y = 12 and 5x − 3y = 4 is (x, y). What is the value of x? (Student-produced response.)
cards.a: 64/41 (≈ 1.5610). Desmos: type both equations and click the intersection, which shows about (1.561, 1.268). Enter 64/41, or a decimal that fills the space: 1.560 (truncated) or 1.561 (rounded). By hand: multiply by 3 and 7 and add: 6x + 35x = 36 + 28, so 41x = 64.
cards.h: → the exact value + the entries Bluebook takes
cards.n: Typing 1.56 from a glance at Desmos: a non-terminating decimal must fill all the spaces (5 characters for a positive answer), so 1.56 is marked wrong.

cards.q: What is the sum of the solutions to |3x − 4| = 11?
cards.a: 8/3. Two cases: 3x − 4 = 11 gives x = 5; 3x − 4 = −11 gives x = −7/3. The sum is 5 − 7/3 = 8/3. Enter 8/3, 2.666 or 2.667.
cards.n: Solving only the positive case and entering 5; an absolute-value equation of this form has two solutions.

cards.q: The graph of the linear function f passes through the points (3, 11) and (7, 23). What is the x-coordinate of the graph's x-intercept?
cards.a: −2/3. The slope is (23 − 11)/(7 − 3) = 3, so f(x) = 3x + b with 11 = 9 + b, b = 2. Setting 3x + 2 = 0 gives x = −2/3. Bluebook accepts −2/3, −.6666, −.6667, −0.666 or −0.667 (a negative answer may use 6 characters, including the sign).
cards.n: Entering −.67 (too few digits) or reporting the y-intercept, 2; the x-intercept is where f(x) = 0.

cards.q:
Which point (x, y) is a solution to the system of inequalities y > 2x − 3 and y ≤ −x + 6?
(A) (3, 3)
(B) (1, 5)
(C) (4, 1)
(D) (0, 7)
cards.a: (B). Test each point. (1, 5): 5 > −1 and 5 ≤ 5, both true (the second holds with equality, which "≤" allows). (A) (3, 3) is where the two boundary lines meet: 3 > 3 is false, because the first inequality is strict. (C) fails 1 > 5. (D) fails 7 ≤ 6.
cards.n: (A) is the intersection of the boundary lines and looks like the "corner" of the region, but it lies on the dashed line (strict >) and is excluded.

cards.q: A car travels at a constant speed of 66 feet per second. What is its speed in miles per hour? (1 mile = 5,280 feet)
cards.a: 45. 66 ft/s × 3,600 s/h = 237,600 ft/h, and 237,600 ÷ 5,280 = 45 mi/h. Setting up the conversion so the units cancel (ft/s × s/h × mi/ft) catches a flipped factor.
cards.n: Multiplying by 60 instead of 3,600 (seconds per minute, not per hour), which gives 0.75.

cards.q: Student-produced response rules: how do you enter an answer of 3½, and which of these entries for 2/3 are accepted: 2/3, .6666, .6667, 0.666, 0.667, .66, .67, 0.67?
cards.a: Enter 3½ as 7/2 or 3.5, never as a mixed number (Bluebook's directions say to convert it). For 2/3, the accepted entries are 2/3, .6666, .6667, 0.666 and 0.667; .66, .67 and 0.67 are rejected because a non-terminating decimal must fill the available space (5 characters for a positive answer, 6 for a negative one, counting the sign). No $, % or commas.
cards.h: → the mixed-number rule + which entries pass
cards.n: 0.67 looks like a perfectly good rounding; it is marked wrong because it does not use all the characters available.

cards.q: What is the sum of all solutions to the equation √(x + 7) = x − 5?
cards.a: 9. Square both sides: x + 7 = x² − 10x + 25, so x² − 11x + 18 = 0 and x = 2 or x = 9. Check each in the original: x = 9 gives √16 = 4 = 9 − 5 ✓; x = 2 gives √9 = 3, but 2 − 5 = −3 ✗, so 2 is extraneous. The only solution is 9, and the sum is 9. Desmos: graph y = √(x + 7) and y = x − 5; they cross once, at x = 9.
cards.h: → value + check each root in the original
cards.n: Entering 11, the sum of both roots of the squared equation; squaring creates a root where the right side is negative.

cards.a: (D). Multiply by (x − 3): x − 2(x − 3) = 3, so −x + 6 = 3 and x = 3. But x = 3 makes the denominators zero, so it is extraneous, and the equation has no solution. Desmos agrees: the graphs of both sides never meet.
cards.h: → letter + check the root against the denominators
cards.n: (A) is the value the algebra produces; any root that zeroes a denominator must be thrown out.

cards.q: The function f is defined by f(x) = −2x² + 12x − 7. What is the maximum value of f(x)?
cards.a: 11. The vertex is at x = −b/(2a) = −12/(−4) = 3, and f(3) = −18 + 36 − 7 = 11. Desmos: graph f and click the vertex, which shows (3, 11); the maximum VALUE is the y-coordinate.
cards.n: Entering 3, the x-coordinate where the maximum occurs; "maximum value of f(x)" asks for the output.

cards.q:
A car is bought for 28,000 dollars. Its value decreases by 15% every 6 months. Which function gives the value V, in dollars, t years after purchase?
(A) V = 28,000(0.85)^(t/2)
(B) V = 28,000(0.70)^t
(C) V = 28,000(0.7225)^t
(D) V = 28,000(0.85)^t
cards.a: (C). There are two 6-month periods per year, so V = 28,000(0.85)^(2t) = 28,000(0.85²)^t = 28,000(0.7225)^t. (B) assumes two 15% drops add up to 30%, but the second 15% comes off a smaller value (a 27.75% yearly drop). (A) inverts the exponent (one drop every two years). (D) is one drop a year.
cards.n: (B) treats percent changes as additive; each 15% is taken from the new, smaller base.

cards.q: How many solutions does the system y = x² − 4x + 7 and y = 2x − 2 have?
cards.a: 1. Set the expressions equal: x² − 4x + 7 = 2x − 2, so x² − 6x + 9 = 0, which is (x − 3)² = 0. The discriminant is 36 − 36 = 0, so there is exactly one solution, (3, 4): the line is tangent to the parabola. Desmos shows the line just touching the parabola at (3, 4).
cards.n: At a zoomed-out Desmos view, a tangent line and a line that barely misses (0) or barely crosses (2) look alike; confirm with the discriminant.

cards.q: In the equation 4x² − 12x + c = 0, c is a constant. For what value of c does the equation have exactly one real solution?
cards.a: 9. Exactly one real solution means the discriminant is zero: (−12)² − 4(4)(c) = 144 − 16c = 0, so c = 9. Check: 4x² − 12x + 9 = (2x − 3)². Desmos: graph y = 4x² − 12x + c, let Desmos make a slider for c, and find where the vertex just touches the x-axis; confirm with the discriminant.
cards.n: Trusting a slider by eye: the default step may skip the exact value, and "touching" is hard to judge; the discriminant gives the exact c.

cards.q:
If x² > 16, which of the following must be true?
(A) x > 4
(B) x < −4
(C) x³ > 64
(D) |x| > 4
cards.a: (D). x² > 16 holds exactly when x > 4 or x < −4, which is |x| > 4. (A) and (C) fail for x = −5 (x² = 25 > 16, but −5 < 4 and (−5)³ = −125). (B) fails for x = 5. Each could be true; only (D) must be.
cards.h: → letter + a counterexample for each other choice
cards.n: (A) is what you get by "taking the square root of both sides" and forgetting the negative branch; test a negative value before choosing.

cards.q:
The graph of y = f(x) is a parabola with vertex (2, −5). What is the vertex of the graph of y = f(x + 3) − 1?
(A) (5, −6)
(B) (5, −4)
(C) (−1, −4)
(D) (−1, −6)
cards.a: (D). Replacing x with x + 3 shifts the graph 3 units LEFT: x = 2 becomes x = −1. Subtracting 1 outside shifts it down 1: y = −5 becomes −6. The vertex is (−1, −6).
cards.n: (A): "+3" feels like a move right; a change inside the function moves the graph opposite to its sign.

cards.q: The polynomial p is defined by p(x) = 2x³ − 5x² + kx − 4, where k is a constant. When p(x) is divided by x − 3, the remainder is 11. What is the value of k?
cards.a: 2. By the remainder theorem, the remainder when p(x) is divided by x − 3 is p(3): 2(27) − 5(9) + 3k − 4 = 54 − 45 + 3k − 4 = 5 + 3k. Setting 5 + 3k = 11 gives k = 2.
cards.h: → value + evaluate p at the root of the divisor
cards.n: Evaluating p(−3) because the divisor shows "− 3"; the divisor x − 3 is zero at x = 3.

cards.q: What is the product of the solutions to 3x² − 7x = 12?
cards.a: −4. First write the equation as 3x² − 7x − 12 = 0. The product of the roots is c/a = −12/3 = −4. (The discriminant, 49 + 144 = 193, is positive, so there are two real solutions.)
cards.n: Using +12 from the right side and entering 4; the constant term must be moved to the left before reading c.

cards.q:
Which of the following is equivalent to (2x − 1)² − (x + 2)²?
(A) (3x + 1)(x − 3)
(B) (3x − 1)(x + 3)
(C) (x − 3)²
(D) 3x² − 3
cards.a: (A). Expand: (4x² − 4x + 1) − (x² + 4x + 4) = 3x² − 8x − 3 = (3x + 1)(x − 3). Or use a difference of squares: [(2x − 1) − (x + 2)][(2x − 1) + (x + 2)] = (x − 3)(3x + 1). Desmos: graph the original and each choice; only (A) lies exactly on top of it.
cards.h: → letter + expand or factor as a difference of squares
cards.n: (B) has the right numbers with the signs swapped; if you check with Desmos, make sure the curves coincide everywhere, not just near one point.

cards.q:
A population of 500 bacteria doubles every 20 minutes. Which function gives the population P after h hours?
(A) P = 500 · 2^(h/20)
(B) P = 500 · 2^(20h)
(C) P = 500 · 2^(3h)
(D) P = 500 · 3^(2h)
cards.a: (C). There are three 20-minute periods in an hour, so after h hours the population has doubled 3h times: P = 500 · 2^(3h). (A) would be right if h were in minutes. (B) doubles 20 times an hour. (D) triples twice an hour.
cards.n: (A) is the familiar "t over the doubling time" form, but the doubling time is in minutes and h is in hours.

cards.q: A store raises the price of a jacket by 25%. Later, it lowers the new price by 20%. The final price is what percent of the original price?
cards.a: 100. Multiply the factors: 1.25 × 0.80 = 1.00, so the final price is 100% of the original. The 20% decrease is taken from the larger, raised price, so it removes exactly the amount the increase added.
cards.n: Adding the changes (+25 − 20 = +5) and entering 105; successive percent changes multiply, because each one applies to a new base.

cards.q: After a 20% discount, a jacket costs $64. What was the price before the discount?
cards.a: 80. The sale price is 80% of the original: 0.80p = 64, so p = 80. Check: 20% of 80 is 16, and 80 − 16 = 64.
cards.h: → dollars + which base the 20% is of
cards.n: Adding 20% of 64 back on (64 + 12.80 = 76.80); the discount was 20% of the original price, not of the sale price.

cards.q: A town had 2,400 residents in 2020 and 3,000 in 2024. The 2020 population is p% less than the 2024 population. What is the value of p?
cards.a: 20. "Less than the 2024 population" makes 3,000 the base: (3,000 − 2,400)/3,000 = 600/3,000 = 20%. (The 2024 population is 25% MORE than the 2020 population, with 2,400 as the base.)
cards.n: Entering 25, the percent increase from 2020; the base is whatever follows "than."

cards.q:
Students by grade and whether they play an instrument
Grade · Plays · Does not play · Total
10th · 18 · 42 · 60
11th · 27 · 33 · 60
12th · 15 · 45 · 60
Total · 60 · 120 · 180
If a student who plays an instrument is selected at random, what is the probability that the student is in 11th grade?
cards.a: 9/20 (0.45). "A student who plays an instrument" restricts the group to the 60 players, so the denominator is 60: 27/60 = 9/20 = 0.45.
cards.n: Using the grand total (27/180 = 0.15); a "given" condition in the question shrinks the denominator to that row or column total.

cards.q:
Survey responses (some cells are blank)
Group · Yes · No · Total
Juniors · (blank) · 24 · (blank)
Seniors · 38 · (blank) · 95
Total · 94 · (blank) · 175
What percent of the juniors answered yes?
cards.a: 70. Juniors who said yes: 94 − 38 = 56. Total juniors: 175 − 95 = 80. So 56/80 = 70%. (Check: seniors' no = 95 − 38 = 57; total no = 24 + 57 = 81; 94 + 81 = 175.)
cards.h: → percent + fill the cells from the totals
cards.n: Dividing by the grand total (56/175 = 32%) or by the yes total (56/94); "percent of the juniors" means juniors are the base.

cards.q: A scatterplot of data has the line of best fit y = 1.8x + 12. One of the data points is (15, 43). How much greater is the actual y-value of this point than the y-value predicted by the line of best fit?
cards.a: 4. The line predicts y = 1.8(15) + 12 = 39 at x = 15. The data point's actual y-value is 43, so it is 43 − 39 = 4 greater (the point lies 4 units above the line).
cards.n: Answering 39 or 43 instead of the difference; questions say "the line of best fit predicts" or "the data show" on purpose, so mark which one you are asked about.

cards.q:
A scatterplot shows the age x, in years, and the price y, in dollars, of 25 used cars of one model. The line of best fit is y = −1,250x + 21,000. Which is the best interpretation of −1,250 in this context?
(A) For each additional year of age, the predicted price of a car decreases by $1,250.
(B) Each car in the data set lost exactly $1,250 in value per year.
(C) The predicted price of a new car is $1,250.
(D) The predicted price decreases by 1,250 percent each year.
cards.a: (A). The slope of a line of best fit describes the model's prediction, in the units of y per unit of x: $1,250 less predicted price per year of age. (B) turns a model into a claim about every car; actual cars scatter around the line. (C) confuses the slope with the y-intercept, $21,000. (D) treats a dollar amount as a percent.
cards.h: → letter + slope as predicted change per unit
cards.n: (B) sounds precise, but "exactly" and "each car" describe the data, not the fitted line; the line gives predicted values.

cards.q: The mean of 8 numbers is 15. When a ninth number is added, the mean of the 9 numbers is 16. What is the ninth number?
cards.a: 24. Work with totals, not means: the 8 numbers total 8 × 15 = 120, and the 9 numbers total 9 × 16 = 144. The ninth number is 144 − 120 = 24.
cards.n: Entering 16 or 17 by nudging the mean; the new number must equal the new mean (16) plus 1 for each of the other 8 numbers it lifts: 16 + 8 = 24.

cards.q:
A data set contains 11 different values. The largest value is increased by 20. Which statement must be true?
(A) The mean and the median both increase.
(B) The median increases, and the mean does not change.
(C) The mean increases, and the median does not change.
(D) Neither the mean nor the median changes.
cards.a: (C). The sum rises by 20, so the mean rises by 20/11 ≈ 1.82. The median is the 6th value in order, and increasing the largest value keeps it the largest, so the middle value is unchanged.
cards.h: → letter + what each measure depends on
cards.n: (A) assumes every average reacts to every value; the median depends only on the middle position.

cards.q:
The table shows values of a quadratic function f.
x · 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · 5
f(x) · 4 · 9 · 18 · 31 · 48
What is the value of f(10)?
cards.a: 193. Desmos: enter a table with columns x₁ and y₁, then type y₁ ~ ax₁² + bx₁ + c. Desmos returns a = 2, b = −1, c = 3 with R² = 1, so f(x) = 2x² − x + 3 and f(10) = 200 − 10 + 3 = 193. By hand: second differences are 4, so a = 2; then use two points for b and c.
cards.n: Typing "=" instead of "~", or y instead of y₁: Desmos then graphs a new function with sliders instead of fitting the table.

cards.q: A printer prints 18 pages per minute. At this rate, how many hours will it take to print 4,860 pages?
cards.n: Entering 270, the time in minutes; the question asks for hours, so finish the conversion.

cards.q:
In a random sample of 500 of a town's registered voters, 62% support a proposed measure. The margin of error for this estimate is 4 percentage points. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
(A) Exactly 62% of the town's registered voters support the measure.
(B) 4% of the respondents answered the survey incorrectly.
(C) It is plausible that between 58% and 66% of all voters in the state support the measure.
(D) It is plausible that between 58% and 66% of the town's registered voters support the measure.
cards.a: (D). A margin of error gives a range of plausible values for the population the sample was drawn from: 62 ± 4, or 58% to 66%, of the town's registered voters. (A) ignores sampling variability. (C) extends the result to a population that was not sampled (the state). (B) misreads what a margin of error measures.
cards.h: → letter + the right population and the ± range
cards.n: (C) has the right numbers, so it passes a quick check; a sample supports conclusions only about the population it was drawn from.

cards.q: The equation of a circle in the xy-plane is x² + y² − 6x + 8y = 11. What is the radius of the circle?
cards.a: 6. Complete the square: (x² − 6x + 9) + (y² + 8y + 16) = 11 + 9 + 16, so (x − 3)² + (y + 4)² = 36. The radius is √36 = 6, and the center is (3, −4).
cards.n: Entering √11 (forgetting to add 9 and 16 to the right side) or 36 (r² instead of r).

cards.q: Two right circular cones are similar. The height of the larger cone is 3 times the height of the smaller cone. The volume of the smaller cone is 40 cubic centimeters. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the larger cone?
cards.a: 1,080. For similar solids, lengths scale by k, areas by k², and volumes by k³. Here k = 3, so the volume scales by 27: 40 × 27 = 1,080. Enter 1080 (no comma).
cards.h: → value + which power of the scale factor
cards.n: Multiplying by 3 (120) or 9 (360); volume is three-dimensional, so the factor is cubed.

cards.q: In right triangle ABC, angle C is the right angle, and sin A = 0.28. What is the value of cos B?
cards.a: 0.28. A and B are complementary (A + B = 90°), and the sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement: cos B = sin(90° − B) = sin A = 0.28. (Both are the ratio of the side opposite A to the hypotenuse.) Enter 0.28, .28 or 7/25.
cards.n: Entering 0.96, which is cos A; the question asks for cos B, the complement.

cards.q: A circle has radius 12. An arc of the circle has a central angle of 150°. The length of the arc is kπ. What is the value of k?
cards.n: Using the area formula instead and entering 60 (the sector's area is 60π); an arc is part of the circumference.

cards.q: What is the value of sin(7π/6)?
cards.a: −1/2. 7π/6 is 210°, in the third quadrant, where sine is negative. Its reference angle is π/6 (30°), and sin(π/6) = 1/2, so sin(7π/6) = −1/2. Enter -1/2, -.5 or -0.5. Desmos works in radians by default; if it has been switched to degrees, sin(7π/6) gives the wrong value.
cards.n: Entering 1/2 from the reference angle alone; the quadrant sets the sign.

cards.q: A tank shaped like a rectangular prism measures 2 feet by 3 feet by 1.5 feet. What is the volume of the tank in cubic inches? (1 foot = 12 inches)
cards.a: 15,552. The volume is 2 × 3 × 1.5 = 9 cubic feet. One cubic foot is 12 × 12 × 12 = 1,728 cubic inches, so 9 × 1,728 = 15,552. Enter 15552 (no comma; it uses all 5 characters). Or convert each edge first: 24 × 36 × 18 = 15,552.
cards.n: Multiplying 9 by 12 (108) or 144 (1,296); a volume conversion uses the factor cubed.

cards.q: Points A, B, and C lie on a circle with center O. Central angle AOB measures 110°, and point C lies on the major arc AB. What is the measure, in degrees, of inscribed angle ACB?
cards.a: 55. An inscribed angle is half the central angle that intercepts the same arc. Angle ACB intercepts minor arc AB, whose central angle is 110°, so angle ACB = 55°. (If C were on the minor arc, the angle would intercept the major arc, 250°, and measure 125°.)
cards.n: Entering 110, the central angle; an inscribed angle is half of it.

cards.q: An equilateral triangle has sides of length 10. Its area is k√3. What is the value of k?
cards.a: 25. The height of an equilateral triangle with side s is (s√3)/2 = 5√3 (a 30-60-90 triangle with short leg 5). Area = ½ × 10 × 5√3 = 25√3, so k = 25. (Formula: area = (√3/4)s² = (√3/4)(100).)
cards.n: Forgetting the ½ and entering 50.

cards.q: In the xy-plane, the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 25 and the line y = x + 2 intersect at two points. What is the greatest x-coordinate of these points?
cards.a: 2. Desmos: graph both and click the two intersections, (−3, −1) and (2, 4); the greater x-coordinate is 2. By substitution: (x − 2)² + (x + 3)² = 25 gives 2x² + 2x − 12 = 0, so x² + x − 6 = 0 and x = 2 or x = −3.
cards.n: Entering 4, the y-coordinate of the same point; Desmos shows (x, y), and the question asks for x.
